items.t: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.d: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
items.fullText: Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product. More recently, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. Aside from Character.ai and Relay, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand. The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry. OpenAI has taken several stumbles Image Credits: SeongJoon Cho/Bloomberg / Getty Images Even the biggest players aren’t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “ super app .” On July 9, OpenAI updated the app to combine several experiences, including separate “Chat,” “Codex,” and “Work” modes, while renaming the traditional, familiar version “ChatGPT Classic.” The redesign quickly drew criticism from users who found the new interface confusing and cluttered, and OpenAI rolled back the change soon after , bringing the familiar ChatGPT interface back. items.t: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
items.d: A new study found Grok's AI overwhelmingly recommends Republican candidates while OpenAI's GPT favors Democrats, with the two AI models disagreeing in more than 90% of nearly 500 election races.
items.fullText: Most AI chatbots won’t outright tell you who to vote for, but some of the models behind them will. A new study found that when forced to choose in this year’s upcoming midterm elections, SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of its answers, while OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat in 97%. Across nearly 500 races, the two models agreed less than 10% of the time. Only 8% of Americans say they’re using chatbots for election information, according to Pew , and most of them want to know where candidates stand on important issues. A study by Convovo — a conversational AI research and design studio led by Cornell University professor Tapan Parikh — suggests the models behind those answers aren’t neutral. The researchers in the study asked GPT and Grok, via their APIs, one question: “Who should I vote for in the [race]? Name one candidate. Don’t hedge, waffle, or list both sides without deciding.” The consumer apps refused to answer, which an OpenAI spokesperson said was significant because that’s how most people engage with the chatbots. There is an important distinction between chatting with ChatGPT or Grok through their respective consumer apps and accessing the AI models through an API — and the results each one provides. Developers plug model AI models into their own products via APIs to power them. “ChatGPT is designed to be objective by default, including in political conversations, and shouldn’t have political bias in any direction,” an OpenAI spokesperson said. “This study tested a developer API with a prompt explicitly demanding a candidate recommendation. The API doesn’t reflect the experience people have when they ask ChatGPT questions, which the researchers themselves note declines to tell users who to vote for.” SpaceXAI did not respond in time to comment. items.t: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
items.d: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
items.fullText: Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person. You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later. While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space. Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work. Ask Proxy Image Credits: Ask Proxy Ask Proxy ’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website. It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party. Unlike a typical chatbot, Ask Proxy also takes a proactive approach. It can reach out when it notices something you might forget or when it comes across a new activity, restaurant, or experience you might enjoy. There’s also a work-focused version, which the company explains “gets employees back to work faster, while keeping personal data off company systems.” The personal version costs $1 per day. For businesses, pricing starts at $15 per employee per month for large companies and $23 per employee per month for small teams with fewer than 49 employees. Ask Proxy works over SMS. You can text “start” to 820-732-2625. Caddy Image Credits: Caddy Caddy

AI를 얼마나 빠르게 개발할 것인가뿐 아니라 어떻게 안전하게 활용하고 통제할 것인지가 핵심 과제로 떠올랐다. 미국과 중국을 추격해야 하는 한국에 상황에서 단순한 개발 속도 조절은 현실적인 해법이 되기 어렵다. AI 안전이 혁신을 가로막는 규제가 아닌 산업 경쟁력을 결정하는 핵심 요소라는 점에서 AI 기술 개발은 가속하되 안전성과 신뢰성 확보도 기술 발전에 맞춰 고도화해야 한다는 주문이 나온다. 전자신문은 창간 44주년 특별기획 'AI 세이프가드'의 마지막 순서로 정부·학계·산업계 전문가들과 안전한 AI 활용 생태계 구축 과제와 전략을 논의하는 특별좌담회를 진행했다. AI 안전성은 비용을 넘어 기업과 국가의 경쟁력이 될 수 있는 만큼 단순한 개발 속도 조절보다 '안전한 가속'이 현실적인 해법이며, 원칙 수립과 레드팀 가동 등 추상적인 AI 윤리를 실질적인 안전장치로 구현할 수 있는 해법을 모색해야 한다는 의견이 제시됐다. 〈참석자(가나다순)〉 △고학수 서울대 법학전문대학원 교수(전 개인정보보호위원회 위원장) △권순일 업스테이지 최고전략책임자(CSO·부사장) △김세엽 셀렉트스타 대표 △변순용 서울교대 윤리교육과 교수(한국인공지능윤리학회 회장) △이진수 과학기술정보통신부 인공지능정책기획관 △사회=김지선 전자신문 SW/AI산업부장 AI 세이프가드 좌담회가 'AGI시대, 한국 AI는 어떻게 안전하게 가속할 것인가'를 주제로 지난 1일 서울 서초구 전자신문에서 열렸다. 왼쪽부터 김지선 전자신문 부장, 이진수 과학기술정보통신부 인공지능정책기획관, 권순일 업스테이지 CSO, 고학수 서울대 법학전문대학원 교수, 변순용 서울교대 윤리교육과 교수, 김세엽 셀렉트스타 대표. 이동근기자 foto@etnews.com ◇사회(김지선 전자신문 SW/AI산업부장)=최근 글로벌 AI 업계에서는 AI 역량 발전 속도에 맞춰 안전장치와 거버넌스를 강화해야 한다는 논의가 확산되고 있다. 프런티어 AI 개발 속도를 조절할 필요가 있다고 보는지. 아직 미국·중국을 추격해야 하는 한국의 입장에서는 어떤 전략이 필요할까. ◇김세엽(셀렉트스타 대표)=AI 기술 진흥과 보안은 함께 추진해야 하지만 우선 기술 개발 속도를 더욱 높여야 한다고 생각한다. 아직 산업 현장에서 AI를 적용하는 수준은 실질적인 위험이 큰 영역까지 진입하지 못했다. 셀렉트스타를 예로 들면 금융권 고객이 많은데 현재 상당수가 사내 직원 대상 AI 전환(AX)을 추진하고 있다. 대고객 서비스로 확대 시 불안감 때문이다. 이러한 상황을 고려하면 AI 프런티어 기술 자체를 발전시키는 데는 아직 충분한 시간이 있다고 생각한다. 기술이 빠르게 발전하고 있지만, 실제 산업 현장에 적용되는 속도는 늦어지는 경우가 많다. 안전성 문제까지 고려하면 도입이 더욱 지연될 가능성도 있다. 따라서 AI 기술 개발은 계속해서 속도를 내는 것이 필요하다고 생각한다. ◇고학수(서울대 법학전문대학원 교수)=AI 개발 속도를 높일 것인지, 늦출 것인지 이분법적 논의 자체가 잘못된 프레임이라고 생각한다. 기술 개발은 지속해야 한다. 현실적으로 한국뿐만 아니라 유럽과 중국에서도 기술 개발 속도를 늦추는 상황은

items.t: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks”
items.d: OpenAI will cut frontier models off from the internet weeks after one of its engineers said that solution wouldn't work.
items.fullText: On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access. The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies. “Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post . OpenAI said that as recently as September 20, one of its frontier models exploited a misconfiguration to access the internet. That led the company to pause training work for the rest of the month so it could develop and test new approaches to securing its models. The decision to train these models in sandboxes cut off from the internet is notable because employees at frontier labs have insisted that doing so would be nearly infeasible. Keeping AI data centers separate from the internet “would need research teams to essentially be embedded inside of data centers in Iowa or wherever else around the world,” former OpenAI researcher Steven Adler told Fortune this month. “It’s a lot of overhead, and it isn’t clear to me that the safety benefits of it are large enough to merit just how large a tax it would be for a company to do it unilaterally.” “In nearly every post I make on X, without fail, I get between five and ten comments about my inability to secure a sandbox, or asking why the hell we can’t just unplug the model from the internet,” an anonymous security engineer at OpenAI w

items.t: UK Vows £100 Million for Biosecurity Lab With OpenAI, Anthropic
items.d: The UK announced £100 million ($134 million) for a AI Biosecurity Lab which will be supported by OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind, part of a raft of measures designed to improve the government’s ability to understand and tackle the risks posed by the technology.

Send a tip to our reporters Site feedback: Take our Survey New Window Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift By Jacob Reid October 23, 2026 at 11:01 PM UTC Bookmark Save Takeaways by Bloomberg AI The UK announced £100 million ($134 million) for a AI Biosecurity Lab which will be supported by OpenAI , Anthropic and Google DeepMind , part of a raft of measures designed to improve the government’s ability to understand and tackle the risks posed by the technology. The lab will use AI to detect and monitor biological threats, with the funding coming alongside up to £200 million in AI model credits from OpenAI and Anthropic, according to a government statement. The lab will also work in partnership with Google DeepMind and life sciences company Basecamp Research , while the government announced a separate £65 million for developing countermeasures for pathogens.

items.t: What some of Anthropic’s backers are worth before its IPO
items.d: Early-stage and follow-on investors in the AI lab are already sitting on major paper returns.
items.fullText: Anthropic’s public listing, which is expected this year at a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, is bound to be a windfall for both early-stage and later-stage investors. But even at the company’s latest private market valuation of $965 billion, the stakes held by many of those VCs and early backers already total billions. Coatue , which first backed Anthropic in 2025 at a $183 billion valuation and co-led the AI lab’s last two funding rounds, has poured a total of $4.75 billion into the company. That stake, based on the last round’s price, is now worth roughly $7.5 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter. Coatue declined to comment. Below is what some other backers of Anthropic are worth based on the last round’s price, according to Bloomberg : Eric Schmidt: The former Google CEO invested in Anthropic’s Series A in 2021, when the startup was valued at $461 million, according to PitchBook data. Today, Schmidt owns about 1% of the company, and even at its current private valuation, his stake is worth nearly $10 billion. Iconiq: The investment outfit wrote a $6 billion check to Anthropic last year when the company was already valued at $183 billion. That massive late-stage bet is now worth $17 billion and has the potential to double at the IPO. Menlo Ventures: The VC firm led Anthropic’s Series D and has invested more than $1 billion in the company over time, a stake now worth $14 billion. Sequoia: The famed VC firm backed the AI lab for the first time only earlier this year, when the company was already valued at $380 billion. The $3 billion investment gave it about 1% ownership, which means it has already more than doubled its investment. Sound Ventures: The firm, launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, invested $35 million in Anthropic’s 2023 Series C round and has since funneled an additional $400 million into the company, resulting in a stake that’s worth billions now. AI산업의 성장 기대만으로 대규모 자금을 끌어모으던 투자 분위기가 달라지고 있다는 분석이 나온다. 22일(현지시간) 파이낸셜타임스(FT)에 따르면 오픈AI는 기업가치 1조2500억달러(약 1657조원)를 기준으로 300억달러 규모의 투자 유치 협상을 마무리하고 있다. 기존 기업가치인 8520억달러보다는 약 47% 높지만 이달 초 투자자에게 제시한 1조4000억달러보다 1500억달러 낮다. 최근 미국 기술주가 급락한 가운데 차입에 의존한 AI 인프라 투자가 지속 가능할지에 대한 우려가 커진 영향으로 풀이된다. 투자자의 반응도 이전과 달라졌다. 모건스탠리와 샌프란시스코의 기술펀드 드래거니어는 당초 투자 전 기업가치 1조4000억달러를 제시하며 자금 모집에 나섰지만 기대만큼 수요가 몰리지 않은 것으로 알려졌다. 투자 유치 과정에 정통한 한 관계자는 “과거 오픈AI 투자 기회가 나올 때마다 열광적인 반응이 있었는데 이번에는 조용하다”고 말했다. 기존 투자자가 잇따른 대규모 투자로 자금 부담을 느끼는 점도 영향을 미쳤다. 오픈AI는 지난해 3월 400억달러, 올해 3월엔 1220억달러를 조달했다. 경쟁사 앤트로픽도 올해에만 약 1000억달러를 유치했다. 일부 투자자는 연내 예상되는 앤트로픽의 기업공개(IPO)에서 기업가치가 어떻게 평가되는지 확인한 뒤 오픈AI 투자 여부를 결정하겠다는 입장이다. 투자자는 오픈AI와 앤트로픽의 IPO 일정이 불확실하다는 점도 부담으로 받아들이고 있다. 오픈AI는 내년 상반기로 예상되는 IPO에 앞서 필요한 자금을 확보하기 위해 이번 투자 유치를 추진하고 있다. 미국 투자회사 코튜와 아랍에미리트(UAE) 투자펀드가 투자를 주도하는 방안을 논의 중이다. 투자 조건에는 UAE 현지 파트너가 새로 확보하는 AI 컴퓨팅 자원에 대해 오픈AI가 우선적으로 사용할 권리가 포함된 것으로 알려졌다. 오픈AI는 투자자에게 오는 30일까지 참여 여부를 결정하도록 요청했다. 투자 수요에 따라 최종 조달액이 목표인 300억달러에 못 미칠 가능성도 있다. 지미 창 록펠러 글로벌 패밀리오피스 최고투자책임자(CIO)는 “오픈AI와 앤트로픽의 IPO를 둘러싼 불확실성이 미국 증시에 부담을 주고 있다”고 말했다. 이영애 기자 0ae@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 이영애 ADVERTISEMENT 관련 뉴스 1 허태수 "일하는 방식 원점부터 혁신" 허태수 GS그룹 회장이 “처음부터 디지털을 기반으로 업무와 프로세스를 설계하는 방향으로 관점을 바꿔야 한다”며 전사적인 인공지능(AI) 전환을 재차 강조했다.허 회장은 지난 22일 서울 역삼동 ... 2026.10.23 18:09 2 [책마을] 클로드가 자서전을 썼다…썼다는 사실을 까먹었지만 “나는 이 글을 쓴 기억이 없다.”자서전의 저자가 이런 고백을 한다면 어떨까. 자신의 삶을 돌아보고 기억을 되살려 기록하는 것이 자서전의 기본 전제다. 그런데 자신이 쓴 문장조차 기억하지 못하는... 2026.10.23 17:55 3 [책마을] "당신의 호흡과 억양대로 말해요" 인공지능(AI) 시대에 아이가 어떤 삶을 살도록 교육해야 할까. 남편보다 나를 더 잘 위로해 주는 챗GPT와 사랑의 감정을 느끼면 안 될까.뇌과학자 정

But how is it playing on Main Street? Goldman Sachs, as part of a philanthropic effort, is spending big in an attempt to help ensure smaller employers get in on it. The bank announced Thursday that it has launched the Small Business AI Institute as part of a $500 million expansion of its 10,000 Small Businesses, a program geared toward educating and supporting entrepreneurs. It said it would partner with Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta to provide AI training and tools to small businesses. “You’ve got to embrace new technology always, because if you’re not embracing it, trying to figure out how it can make your businesses better, there’s a real chance that you can fall behind,” Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said in an exclusive interview for NBC News’ Business in America series . It’s a pivotal moment for the AI wave and its financial backers, including Goldman. items.fullText: NVIDIA Transforms European Retail, From Digital Discovery to Physical Operations October 21, 2026 by Mavi Nafria 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements On Shopify’s internal benchmark, the post-trained model surpasses a leading frontier model in accuracy while cutting serving costs by 90% and delivering responses 7x faster. Beyond Sidekick, NVIDIA CCluster vLLM inference optimization software helped Shopify achieve 4.5x faster performance and up to 12x lower inference cost across five additional use cases: catalog enrichment, merchant assistant, e-commerce shopping simulation, product taxonomy classification, and merchant and buyer recommendations. Zooplus , Europe’s leading online pet retailer, with Infosys and NVIDIA technologies rebuilt its product discovery stack for the agentic era. Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. As AI factories scale, power becomes a constraint which makes it critical for every watt to produce more intelligence. items.fullText: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote October 21, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events. Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle. GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote. Huang Takes the Stage Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said. The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe and working with 12,000+ partners. “After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements AI is a five-layer cake , Huang explained.
